subject: Github won't let me be a pusher!

messages.author: 0c39e60ddb38622b
messages.subject: Github won't let me be a pusher!
parts:
Hi:

I'm trying to push some changes to my forked ggplot2 repository on
Github. Several hours ago, I tried to push and got a dialog box that
asked for my user ID and a follow-up one for my password. Alas, I gave
an incorrect password (I think I found the right one now) and
subsequent attempts to push end up with a 403 error (disallowed
access). I haven't been able to get another login try. Any ideas?

Dennis (da** newbie)

messages.author: dc06d729e023580a
messages.subject: Re: Github won't let me be a pusher!
parts:
I don't think you should be asked for a password. Did you set up your
ssh keys as described at http://help.github.com/set-up-git-redirect ?

Hadley

messages.author: d34d025a513c07fc
messages.subject: Re: Github won't let me be a pusher!
parts:
Maybe this will help?
http://stackoverflow.com/questions/7438313/pushing-to-git-returning-error-code-403-fatal-http-request-failed

Short version: if you cloned the https:// address, it's read-only (I think that's why you're getting a HTTP error code number instead of some other error). You need to use the ssh:// or git:// address instead.

You should be able to edit your .git/config file and use that address instead of the https address. Under the remote="origin" section, change the value for url:
  url = g...@github.com:myuser/ggplot2.git

This should make it connect using the git protocol.

-Winston
